title: Affine open complements are finite on Noetherian integral curves
statement: Let $X$ be an integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] scheme [def-pc-scheme] of topological Krull dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For every nonempty affine open subscheme $U$ of $X$, the complement $X\setminus U$ is a finite set of points.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09ND, proof, sentence 'Since X is Noetherian, each of the sets X \setminus U_i is finite'

proof.text: Because $U$ is open, its complement $E:=X\setminus U$ is closed. Since $U$ is nonempty, the hypotheses of the point-outside-open lemma apply to every $x\in E$.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09ND, proof, setup before the sentence 'Since X is Noetherian'

proof.text: For each $x\in E$, [lem-sc-dim-one-point-outside-open-closed] gives that $\{x\}$ is closed in $X$. Its hypotheses hold: $X$ is irreducible because it is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]; $X$ is Kolmogorov, since for $y\neq z$ in $X$ the closures $\overline{\{y\}}$, $\overline{\{z\}}$ are irreducible closed subsets with generic points $y$ and $z$, hence distinct by the uniqueness of generic points in [lem-sc-scheme-sober], so one of the points, say $z$, is not in the closure of the other and the open set $X\setminus\overline{\{y\}}$ contains $z$ but not $y$; $X$ has topological Krull dimension $1\leq1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; and $U$ is a nonempty open subset with $x\notin U$.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09ND, proof, second sentence and the dimension-one point argument

proof.text: Thus every point of the closed subset $E$ is closed in $X$. Applying [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-points-finite] to $E$ shows that $E=X\setminus U$ is finite.

source.place: Properties Lemma 0BA8, conclusion that a closed subset all of whose points are closed is finite

proof_origin.place: Varieties Lemma 09ND, proof, sentence 'Since X is Noetherian, each of the sets X \setminus U_i is finite', with Properties Lemma 0BA8
